packageRegistries.help: The registries every Node and Python source of this organization installs from, for its own code and its dependencies. Each field can hold a value or a secret reference such as ${secret:npm_token}. The public npm registry and the public PyPI need no entry.
packageRegistries.npmHelp: A registry with a scope serves that scope's packages. The mirror serves every other package.
packageRegistries.npmNone: No npm registries. Packages come from the public npm registry.
packageRegistries.pypiHelp: The indexes Python sources install their packages from. The default index serves every Python install in place of the public PyPI.
packageRegistries.pypiNone: No PyPI indexes. Packages come from the public PyPI.
packageRegistries.gitHelp: The hosts Node and Python sources fetch Git code and Git dependencies from.
packageRegistries.scopeHelp: For example @acme. Leave empty for a registry with no scope.
packageRegistries.npmCredentialHelp: An access token, or user:password, for example an Artifactory user and its API key.
packageRegistries.pypiCredentialHelp: An access token, or user:password, for example an Artifactory user and its API key.
packageRegistries.gitCredentialHelp: A token alone is sent as x-access-token, as GitHub expects. Otherwise enter user:token. GitLab: any username. Bitbucket Cloud: x-token-auth for repository or workspace access tokens, or your username or email for API tokens. Bitbucket Data Center: your username, or x-token-auth for project or repository tokens.
packageRegistries.mirrorHelp: Every package without a scope of its own is installed through this registry. An organization has one npm mirror.
packageRegistries.pypiMirrorHelp: Every Python package is installed from this index instead of the public PyPI. An organization has one default index.
packageRegistries.gitHostHelp: The host, with its port and path where the server has them, for example bitbucket.example.com:7990/bitbucket.
packageRegistries.caBundleHelp: Only for a server whose certificate is signed by your own authority, such as an Artifactory proxy inside your network: its PEM certificate, or a secret reference. It is trusted beside the public authorities. Leave empty otherwise.
